english_classification.chapter_title: Concerning the Cross of Light: [...] trample upon it.
english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter contains essentially no oldest teaching substrate. The 'Cross of Light' — divine substance trapped in vegetation and matter — is a cosmological concept with substrate roots, but it is REFERENCED and APPLIED here, never systematically expounded. The chapter never maps the Cross of Light's structure, correspondences, or place in the cosmic hierarchy. Instead, it is a fully institutional/pastoral chapter: a disciple asks about inadvertent sin while performing church duties (traveling on missions, gathering alms), and Mani responds with pastoral counsel and an extended doctor analogy. Teaching purity is the lowest observed (0.172). Strong editorial fatigue confirms later-layer dominance in second half. Three seam flags fire on institutional paragraphs. The doctor parable (¶7-9, 14) is an elaborate wisdom analogy serving the pastoral argument, not a cosmic-domain→cosmic-domain mapping. The NT citation in ¶10 marks editorial composition. The entire chapter is a product of the institutional/ecclesiastical layer.
